sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Peoria, AZ?
sections.html:
Peoria is a fast-growing city on the northwest side of the Phoenix area, and its limits reach into two counties, which changes where a deed gets recorded. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 200,881 residents, up 5.2 percent from the April 2020 estimate base.

Below you will find the Census numbers, how the city grew, the school districts that cover it, the vacation rental permit rules, the county recording steps and the property tax dates that apply when you sell.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Peoria homes?
sections.html:
Peoria's median owner-occupied home value is $463,600 and its median gross rent is $1,843 for 2020 to 2024, both above the Census Bureau figures for Phoenix and Mesa. The table lists the measures sellers use most.

With 76.0 percent of homes owner-occupied, Peoria is a city of owners. The mean commute is 28.2 minutes, longer than the Mesa, Phoenix or Oro Valley averages in the same Census table.

sections.h2: How did Peoria grow, and where are its main districts?
sections.html:
Peoria began as a settlement in 1886 and is now the ninth-largest city in Arizona by population. The Straw family was the first to establish residency in November 1886, and settlers from Peoria, Illinois chose the name. Grand Avenue, laid out in 1887, linked the town sites of Alhambra, Glendale and Peoria, and the settlers filed the plat with the Maricopa County recorder on May 24, 1897.

A Santa Fe, Prescott and Phoenix spur line reached Peoria between 1891 and 1895. Old Town holds the city's historic buildings, and 83rd Avenue between Bell Road and Thunderbird Road is the entertainment district called P83, next to the Peoria Sports Complex, which is the spring training home of the San Diego Padres and Seattle Mariners.

In the north, the city annexed Lake Pleasant in 1996. The Agua Fria River and New River cross the city, though both usually run dry, and Skunk Creek is a main wash with trails that connect to Glendale. Hills and mountains such as Sunrise Mountain and the Hieroglyphic Mountains sit at the northern end. Peoria is the sixth-largest Arizona city by land area, so two Peoria addresses can feel very different.

Most of Peoria lies inside the Peoria Unified School District, but several other districts cover its edges. The split is worth confirming before you advertise a school zone.

  • Peoria Unified covers most of the city. Its high schools inside Peoria are Peoria (opened 1922), Centennial, Sunrise Mountain and Liberty.
  • The Deer Valley Unified School District serves parts of the northeast, including Terramar and West Wing elementary schools.
  • The Nadaburg Unified School District covers part of the northwest.
  • The Wickenburg Unified School District serves the portion of Peoria in Yavapai County.

Peoria Unified is also the largest employer on the city's 2022 list, with 2,130 employees, followed by the City of Peoria at 1,800. Charter schools operate in the city too.

sections.h2: How do roads, water and climate affect a Peoria house?
sections.html:
Peoria is served by Loop 101, Loop 303 and State Route 74, and Valley Metro buses and the WeRIDE on-demand service cover parts of the city.

Peoria draws much of its water through the Central Arizona Project from Lake Pleasant, and Arizona Public Service supplies most electricity, with some customers served by Salt River Project. Summers run hot: monthly average highs are 104 degrees in July and 105 in August, the record high is 122 degrees, and annual rainfall averages about 9.19 inches. A seller can hand a buyer cooling system service records and roof repair history and answer the first inspection questions before they are asked.

sections.h2: Do Peoria's vacation rental rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the house has been used as a short-term or vacation rental, because Peoria requires a city permit. City Council adopted Ordinance 2022-20 on October 11, 2022, in response to Arizona Senate Bill 1168. The permit application is free.

The city's announcement lists these conditions for keeping a permit active:

  • The owner notifies surrounding neighbors and gives them emergency contact information.
  • The owner carries liability insurance of at least $500,000 and runs sex offender checks on guests, unless an online marketplace already provides them.
  • The city registration number appears on every advertisement.
  • A permit can be suspended for up to 12 months after three verified violations in a rolling 12 months, or one serious infraction.

Call the Code Compliance Division at 623-773-7162 to ask about the permit status of a specific house, and tell your buyer the answer.

sections.h2: What should a Peoria seller gather before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
Collect the papers that tell a buyer which rules apply to the house. A short folder saves days once an offer is on the table.

  • The parcel number and the county it falls in, Maricopa or Yavapai.
  • Any Peoria vacation rental permit number and proof of the insurance behind it.
  • Cooling system service records and the roof's repair history.
  • The most recent property tax statement, so the title company can see what is paid.
  • The name of the school district for the address, taken from the district rather than from memory.

Peoria's population grew from 154,065 in 2010 to 190,985 in 2020, and the city has more than 176 square miles of land, so records vary from one Peoria house to the next.

sections.h2: Which county records a Peoria deed?
sections.html:
Most Peoria houses record with the Maricopa County Recorder, but the part of the city in Yavapai County records there. Ask your title company which recorder applies to your parcel before the closing date.

In Maricopa County a deed must carry an Affidavit of Property Value or an exemption code, and the standard recording fee is $30.00 per document. The recorder takes documents in person at 301 W Jefferson St, Suite 200 in Phoenix, by mail or electronically. Under A.R.S. 11-1133, the affidavit records the sale price, the parcel number, the sale date, the financing type and whether the home is owner-occupied or rented, and the recorder must refuse a deed without a complete one unless an exemption applies.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due on a Peoria house?
sections.html:
Arizona property tax is due in two halves, October 1 and March 1. Under A.R.S. 42-18052, the first half is delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1, which has now passed, and the second half is delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. A bill of $100 or less is due in full on October 1.

Ask the county treasurer where the parcel sits whether the first half is paid, and ask your title company how the year's tax is shared between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Does Peoria require a permit to rent a house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. Peoria's Ordinance 2022-20, adopted October 11, 2022, requires a city permit for vacation and short-term rentals. The permit application is free, and owners must meet notification, insurance and advertising rules.

faqs.q: Is all of Peoria in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: No. Most of Peoria is in Maricopa County, but the northern part of the city extends into Yavapai County. That affects which county recorder, assessor and treasurer handle a given parcel.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Peoria?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports a median value of $463,600 for owner-occupied homes in Peoria for 2020 to 2024. That is a median for the whole city, so any single house can sit well above or below it.
Peoria Unified School District serves most of the city. Deer Valley Unified, Nadaburg Unified and Wickenburg Unified cover other portions, so check the address with the district.

faqs.q: Does a Peoria deed need an Affidavit of Property Value?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the transfer qualifies for an exemption code. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires the affidavit with a recorded deed or sale contract, and the county recorder refuses to record without it unless an exemption is noted.
